### Enforce Data Types

```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

# Convert labelled variables to numeric properly
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    niv_proc = as.numeric(as_factor(niv_proc)) - 1,  # converts 1="Yes", 2="No" to 0/1
    imv_proc = as.numeric(as_factor(imv_proc)) - 1,
    highest_paco2 = as.numeric(highest_paco2),
    abg_ph = as.numeric(abg_ph),
    vbg_co2 = as.numeric(vbg_co2),
    vbg_ph = as.numeric(vbg_ph)
  )


```

## Outcome Definition 1: Vent code & resp acidosis (by ABG or VBG)

Below is my first (probably most stringent) iteration of hypercapnic respiratory failure: co2 greater than 45 if abg, 50 if vbg, ph \<7.35 - they have to have either an abg or a vbg showing this, AND either NIV or IMV or both. I've written it so that ABG values and VBG values cannot mix\

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    gas_source = case_when(
      !is.na(highest_paco2) & !is.na(abg_ph) ~ "ABG",
      TRUE ~ "VBG"
    )
  )

```

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    hrf_hypercapnic = case_when(
      # ABG-based HRF
      (niv_proc == 1 | imv_proc == 1) &
        gas_source == "ABG" &
        highest_paco2 >= 45 &
        abg_ph <= 7.35 ~ 1,

      # VBG-based HRF (only when ABG incomplete)
      (niv_proc == 1 | imv_proc == 1) &
        gas_source == "VBG" &
        !is.na(vbg_co2) & !is.na(vbg_ph) &
        vbg_co2 >= 50 &
        vbg_ph <= 7.35 ~ 1,

      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    hrf_hypercapnic = factor(hrf_hypercapnic, labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  )


```

Counts (bottom right is amount of patients meeting criteria above, adds up to full dataset)

```{r}
table(
  hrf = stata_data$hrf_hypercapnic,
  any_vent = (stata_data$niv_proc == 1 | stata_data$imv_proc == 1)
)

```

Counts for categories of obesity:

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    curr_bmi_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(na_if(as.character(zap_labels(curr_bmi)), "n/a"))
    )
  )

```

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
mutate(
bmi_category = case_when(
is.na(curr_bmi_num) ~ NA_character_,
curr_bmi_num < 18.5 ~ "Underweight",
curr_bmi_num < 25   ~ "Normal weight",
curr_bmi_num < 30   ~ "Overweight",
curr_bmi_num < 35   ~ "Obesity I",
curr_bmi_num < 40   ~ "Obesity II",
curr_bmi_num >= 40  ~ "Obesity III"
)
)

```

```{r}
table(stata_data$hrf_hypercapnic, useNA = "ifany")
summary(stata_data$curr_bmi_num)
table(stata_data$bmi_category, useNA = "ifany")

```

\[BL - note high rates of BMI missing data\]

### Counts for both HRF as defined above AND current BMI above 30

```{r}
stata_data %>%
  filter(
    hrf_hypercapnic == "Yes",
    curr_bmi_num > 30
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_patients = n()
  )

```

Counts for HRF and BMI by category

```{r}
stata_data %>%
  filter(
    hrf_hypercapnic == "Yes",
    !is.na(curr_bmi_num)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    bmi_category = case_when(
      curr_bmi_num < 18.5 ~ "Underweight",
      curr_bmi_num < 25   ~ "Normal",
      curr_bmi_num < 30   ~ "Overweight",
      curr_bmi_num < 35   ~ "Obesity I",
      curr_bmi_num < 40   ~ "Obesity II",
      curr_bmi_num >= 40  ~ "Obesity III"
    )
  ) %>%
  count(bmi_category) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

```

## Regression Analyses for Outcome 1

Below is regression, starting with BMI (the degrees of freedom is 112k which seems appropriate - includes all patients with a BMI and labs/vent indicating NO HRF, plus the patients with BMI and hypercapnic respiratory failure as defined above)

```{r}
stata_hrf_analysis <- stata_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(curr_bmi_num),
         (!is.na(highest_paco2) & !is.na(abg_ph)) |
         (!is.na(vbg_co2) & !is.na(vbg_ph)))
```

### Unadjusted (aka simple) regression for outcome 1

```{r}
logit_bmi_hrf <- glm(hrf_hypercapnic ~ curr_bmi_num,
data = stata_hrf_analysis,
family = binomial)

summary(logit_bmi_hrf)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(logit_bmi_hrf), confint(logit_bmi_hrf)))

```

OR shows small increase in risk with BMI, though is statistically significant

\[BL Edit - though keep in mind, Odds increased by .02 for each BMI point (e.g. 10 = 20% increase in odds)\]

### Adjusted, multivariable regression for outcome 1

Regression done again adjusted for variables NOT influenced by BMI (age, sex, ethnicity included - didn't include location as it appears to be the same for all entries)

```{r}
baseline_model <- glm(
hrf_hypercapnic ~ curr_bmi_num + age_at_encounter + sex + ethnicity,
data = stata_hrf_analysis,
family = binomial
)

summary(baseline_model)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(baseline_model), confint(baseline_model)))
```

Association appears to be stronger once adjusted

### Are proportions of hypercapnic respiratory failure (v1) different across BMI categories?

Just out of curiosity ran Chi square analysis below

```{r}
bmi_hrf_subset <- stata_hrf_analysis %>%
filter(!is.na(bmi_category))
```

```{r}
bmi_hrf_summary <- bmi_hrf_subset %>%
group_by(bmi_category) %>%
summarise(
n_total = n(),
n_hrf = sum(hrf_hypercapnic == "Yes"),
n_no_hrf = sum(hrf_hypercapnic == "No"),
pct_hrf = round(100 * n_hrf / n_total, 1),
pct_no_hrf = round(100 * n_no_hrf / n_total, 1)
) %>%
arrange(factor(bmi_category, levels = c("Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight",
"Obesity I", "Obesity II", "Obesity III")))

chisq_test <- chisq.test(table(bmi_hrf_subset$bmi_category, bmi_hrf_subset$hrf_hypercapnic))

bmi_hrf_summary
chisq_test$p.value
```

Visualization:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Make sure bmi_category is ordered
bmi_hrf_summary <- bmi_hrf_summary %>%
  mutate(bmi_category = factor(bmi_category,
                               levels = c("Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight",
                                          "Obesity I", "Obesity II", "Obesity III")))

# Plot proportion of HRF by BMI category
ggplot(bmi_hrf_summary, aes(x = bmi_category, y = pct_hrf, fill = bmi_category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_hrf, "%")), vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure by BMI Category",
    x = "BMI Category",
    y = "Percent with HRF"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Outcome Definition 2: J96.\*2 ICD code & Respiratory Acidosis (by ABG or VBG)

Regression done with new definition of hypercapnic respiratory failure - pH and CO2 definition as above, except now including (required) ICD codes instead of ventilation (I only used 4 - the first four that are listed in database):

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Lab-based hypercapnic respiratory failure (ABG or VBG)
    hrf_hypercapnic_labs_v2 = case_when(
      !is.na(highest_paco2) & !is.na(abg_ph) &
       highest_paco2 >= 45 & abg_ph < 7.35 ~ 1, # BL note - fixed this 50->45
      
      !is.na(vbg_co2) & !is.na(vbg_ph) &
        vbg_co2 >= 50 & vbg_ph < 7.35 ~ 1,
      
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    
    # ICD-based hypercapnic respiratory failure
    hrf_hypercapnic_icd_v2 = ifelse(
      has_j9612 == 1 |
      has_j9622 == 1 |
      has_j9692 == 1 |
      has_j9602 == 1,
      1, 0
    ),
    
    # Final combined HRF definition (labs OR ICD)
    hrf_hypercapnic_v2 = ifelse(
      hrf_hypercapnic_labs_v2 == 1 |
      hrf_hypercapnic_icd_v2 == 1,
      1, 0
    )
  )

```

```{r}
stata_data <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict = ifelse(
      hrf_hypercapnic_labs_v2 == 1 &
      hrf_hypercapnic_icd_v2  == 1,
      1, 0
    )
  )

```

Number of patients meeting strict definition

```{r}
table(stata_data$hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict, useNA = "ifany")

```

```{r}
stata_hrf_strict_analysis <- stata_data %>%
  mutate(
    has_gas = (!is.na(highest_paco2) & !is.na(abg_ph)) |
              (!is.na(vbg_co2) & !is.na(vbg_ph))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    # Keep strict HRF cases
    hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict == 1 |
      
    # OR clean controls with labs and no HRF by any definition
    (
      has_gas == TRUE &
      hrf_hypercapnic_labs_v2 == 0 &
      hrf_hypercapnic_icd_v2  == 0
    )
  )

```

### Unadjusted Logistic Regression for Outcome 2

```{r}
model_strict_bmi_unadj <- glm(
  hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict ~ curr_bmi_num,
  family = binomial,
  data = stata_hrf_strict_analysis
)

summary(model_strict_bmi_unadj)

or_table <- exp(cbind(
  OR = coef(model_strict_bmi_unadj),
  confint(model_strict_bmi_unadj)
))

or_table

```

### Adjusted, Multivariable Regression for Outcome 2

Then adjusted for age, sex, ethnicity:

```{r}
baseline_model_strict <- glm(
  hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict ~
    curr_bmi_num +
    age_at_encounter +
    sex +
    ethnicity,
  data = stata_hrf_strict_analysis,
  family = binomial
)

summary(baseline_model_strict)

exp(cbind(
  OR = coef(baseline_model_strict),
  confint(baseline_model_strict)
))

```

### Are proportions of hypercapnic respiratory failure (v2) different across BMI categories?

```{r}
# Subset to patients with BMI categories
bmi_hrf_strict_subset <- stata_hrf_strict_analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category))

# Summary table by BMI category
bmi_hrf_strict_summary <- bmi_hrf_strict_subset %>%
  group_by(bmi_category) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_hrf = sum(hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict == 1),
    n_no_hrf = sum(hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict == 0),
    pct_hrf = round(100 * n_hrf / n_total, 1),
    pct_no_hrf = round(100 * n_no_hrf / n_total, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(bmi_category, levels = c("Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight",
                                         "Obesity I", "Obesity II", "Obesity III")))

# Chi-square test
chisq_test_strict <- chisq.test(table(
  bmi_hrf_strict_subset$bmi_category,
  bmi_hrf_strict_subset$hrf_hypercapnic_v2_strict
))

# View summary table and p-value
bmi_hrf_strict_summary
chisq_test_strict$p.value

```

and visualization

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Make sure bmi_category is ordered
bmi_hrf_strict_summary <- bmi_hrf_strict_summary %>%
  mutate(bmi_category = factor(bmi_category,
                               levels = c("Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight",
                                          "Obesity I", "Obesity II", "Obesity III")))

# Plot proportion of strict HRF by BMI category
ggplot(bmi_hrf_strict_summary, aes(x = bmi_category, y = pct_hrf, fill = bmi_category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_hrf, "%")), vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Strict Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure by BMI Category",
    x = "BMI Category",
    y = "Percent with Strict HRF"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```
